Location of Roots and Quadratic Expressions

questions.q: If \(x,y,z\) are all real and distinct then \(u=x^2+4y^2+9z^2-6yz-3zx-2xy\) is always
Let \(a>0\), \(b>0\), and \(c>0\). Then both the roots of the equation \(ax^2+bx+c=0\).
questions.sol: Sum of roots \(-\frac ba<0\), product \(\frac ca>0\). If the roots are real both are negative; if they are complex their common real part is \(-\frac b{2a}<0\). In either case the real parts are negative.

questions.q: Both roots of the equation \((x-b)(x-c)+(x-c)(x-a)+(x-a)(x-b)=0\) are always
questions.sol: The equation is \(3x^2-2(a+b+c)x+(ab+bc+ca)=0\) with \(D=4\left[(a+b+c)^2-3(ab+bc+ca)\right]=2\left[(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2\right]\ge0\).

questions.q: The number of real solutions of the equation \(|x|^2-3|x|+2=0\) is
If \(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n\) are any real numbers and \(n\) is any positive integer, then
questions.sol: The true inequality is \(n\sum x_i^2\ge\left(\sum x_i\right)^2\) (Cauchy–Schwarz). Taking \(x_1=x_2=1\), \(n=2\): (a) \(4<4\), (b) \(2\ge4\), (c) \(2\ge8\) all fail.

questions.q: The largest interval for which \(x^{12}-x^9+x^4-x+1>0\) is
questions.sol: For \(x\le0\) every term is \(\ge0\) and the constant is \(1\). For \(0<x<1\): \(x^{12}+x^4(1-x^5)+(1-x)>0\). For \(x\ge1\): \(x^9(x^3-1)+x(x^3-1)+1>0\). So it is positive for all real \(x\).

questions.q: Two towns \(A\) and \(B\) are \(60\) km apart. A school is to be built to serve \(150\) students in town \(A\) and \(50\) students in town \(B\). If the total distance to be travelled by all \(200\) students is to be as small as possible, then the school should be built at
questions.sol: At distance \(x\) from \(A\) the total distance is \(150x+50(60-x)=3000+100x\), least at \(x=0\).

questions.q: If \(p,q,r\) are any real numbers, then
questions.sol: If \(p\ge q\): \(\frac12(p+q-(p-q))=q\); if \(p<q\) it gives \(p\). So (b) holds. (a) and (c) fail e.g. for \(p=q=r\).

questions.q: If \(a+b+c=0\), then the quadratic equation \(3ax^2+2bx+c=0\) has
opts: One root in \((2,3)\) and the other in \((-2,-1)\)
questions.sol: \(f(x)=ax^3+bx^2+cx\) has \(f(0)=0=f(1)\), so by Rolle's theorem \(f'(x)=3ax^2+2bx+c\) vanishes somewhere in \((0,1)\).

questions.q: The equation \(x-\dfrac2{x-1}=1-\dfrac2{x-1}\) has :
questions.sol: Cancelling the common term gives \(x=1\), but the equation is not defined at \(x=1\). No root.

questions.q: If \(a^2+b^2+c^2=1\), then \(ab+bc+ca\) lies in the interval
questions.sol: \((a+b+c)^2\ge0\) gives \(ab+bc+ca\ge-\frac12\); \(\frac12\sum(a-b)^2\ge0\) gives \(ab+bc+ca\le a^2+b^2+c^2=1\).

questions.q: If \(a,b\) and \(c\) are distinct positive numbers, then the expression \((b+c-a)(c+a-b)(a+b-c)-abc\) is
questions.sol: At most one factor can be negative; then the product is \(\le0<abc\). If all are positive put \(x=b+c-a\), \(y=c+a-b\), \(z=a+b-c\): \(abc=\dfrac{(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)}8\ge xyz\) by AM–GM, with equality only if \(a=b=c\). As \(a,b,c\) are distinct the expression is negative.

questions.q: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the roots of \(x^2+px+q=0\) and \(\alpha^4,\beta^4\) are roots of \(x^2-rx+s=0\), then the equation \(x^2-4qx+2q^2-r=0\) has always
opts: One positive and one negative root.
questions.sol: \(r=\alpha^4+\beta^4\), \(q=\alpha\beta\). Discriminant \(=16q^2-4(2q^2-r)=4(2q^2+r)=4(\alpha^2+\beta^2)^2\ge0\), so the roots are real. Their product \(2q^2-r=-(\alpha^2-\beta^2)^2\le0\) can be zero, so (d) is not always true.

questions.q: Let \(a,b,c\) be real numbers, \(a\ne0\). If \(\alpha\) is a root of \(a^2x^2+bx+c=0\), \(\beta\) is the root of \(a^2x^2-bx-c=0\) and \(0<\alpha<\beta\), then the equation \(a^2x^2+2bx+2c=0\) has a root \(\gamma\) that always satisfies
questions.sol: Let \(f(x)=a^2x^2+2bx+2c\). Using \(b\alpha+c=-a^2\alpha^2\) and \(b\beta+c=a^2\beta^2\): \(f(\alpha)=-a^2\alpha^2<0\), \(f(\beta)=3a^2\beta^2>0\). So \(f\) has a root between \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha,\beta\) be the roots of the equation \((x-a)(x-b)=c\), \(c\ne0\). Then the roots of the equation \((x-\alpha)(x-\beta)+c=0\) are
questions.sol: \((x-a)(x-b)-c=(x-\alpha)(x-\beta)\), so \((x-\alpha)(x-\beta)+c=(x-a)(x-b)\), whose roots are \(a,b\).

questions.q: The number of points of intersection of two curves \(y=2\sin x\) and \(y=5x^2+2x+3\) is
questions.sol: \(5x^2+2x+3\) has minimum \(3-\frac4{20}=2.8>2\ge2\sin x\). The curves never meet.

questions.q: If \(p,q,r\) are \(+\)ve and are in A.P., the roots of quadratic equation \(px^2+qx+r=0\) are all real for
questions.sol: \(q=\frac{p+r}2\) and \(q^2\ge4pr\) give \(p^2-14pr+r^2\ge0\), i.e. \(\left(\frac pr\right)^2-14\frac pr+1\ge0\), i.e. \(\left(\frac pr-7\right)^2\ge48\).

questions.q: Let \(p,q\in\{1,2,3,4\}\). The number of equations of the form \(px^2+qx+1=0\) having real roots is
The equation \(\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}=\sqrt{4x-1}\) has
questions.sol: Squaring: \(2x-2\sqrt{x^2-1}=4x-1\), i.e. \(-2\sqrt{x^2-1}=2x-1\). The domain needs \(x\ge1\), where the right side is positive but the left side is \(\le0\). No solution.

questions.q: The roots of the equation \(x^2-2ax+a^2+a-3=0\) are real and less than \(3\), then
If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) \((\alpha<\beta)\), are the roots of the equation \(x^2+bx+c=0\), where \(c<0<b\), then
questions.sol: \(\alpha\beta=c<0\) gives \(\alpha<0<\beta\); \(\alpha+\beta=-b<0\) gives \(\beta<-\alpha=|\alpha|\).

questions.q: If \(b>a\), then the equation \((x-a)(x-b)-1=0\) has
opts: one root in \((-\infty,a)\) and other in \((b,\infty)\).
questions.sol: \(f(x)=(x-a)(x-b)-1\) opens upward with \(f(a)=f(b)=-1<0\), so \(a\) and \(b\) lie between the roots.

questions.q: For the equation \(3x^2+px+3=0\), \(p>0\), if one of the roots is square of the other, then \(p\) is equal to
questions.sol: Roots \(\alpha,\alpha^2\): \(\alpha^3=1\) and \(\alpha+\alpha^2=-\frac p3\). \(\alpha=1\) gives \(p=-6\); \(\alpha=\omega\) gives \(\omega+\omega^2=-1\), \(p=3\).

questions.q: For all, \(x\in(0,1)\)
questions.sol: \(g(x)=x-\log_e(1+x)\) has \(g(0)=0\), \(g'(x)=\frac x{1+x}>0\), so \(\log_e(1+x)<x\). Also \(e^x>1+x\), \(\sin x<x\) and \(\log_ex<0<x\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha,\beta\) be the roots of \(x^2-x+p=0\) and \(\gamma,\delta\) be the roots of \(x^2-4x+q=0\). If \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\) are in G.P., then the integral value of \(p\) and \(q\) respectively, are
Let \(f(x)=(1+b^2)x^2+2bx+1\) and let \(m(b)\) be the minimum value of \(f(x)\). As \(b\) varies, the range of \(m(b)\) is in
The number of solutions of \(\log_4(x-1)=\log_2(x-3)\) is
questions.sol: \(x-1=(x-3)^2\) gives \(x^2-7x+10=0\), \(x=2,5\); the domain needs \(x>3\), so only \(x=5\).

questions.q: The number of values of \(k\), for which the system of equations \((k+1)x+8y=4k\), \(kx+(k+3)y=3k-1\) has infinitely many solutions is
questions.sol: Need \(\dfrac{k+1}k=\dfrac8{k+3}=\dfrac{4k}{3k-1}\). The first equality gives \(k=1,3\); only \(k=1\) satisfies the second (\(2=2=2\)).

questions.q: If \(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n\) are positive real numbers whose product is a fixed number \(c\), then the minimum value of \(a_1+a_2+\ldots+a_{n-1}+2a_n\) is
questions.sol: AM–GM on the \(n\) numbers \(a_1,\ldots,a_{n-1},2a_n\): sum \(\ge n\left(2a_1a_2\cdots a_n\right)^{1/n}=n(2c)^{1/n}\).

questions.q: The set of all real numbers \(x\) for which \(x^2-|x+2|+x>0\), is
questions.sol: For \(x\ge-2\): \(x^2-2>0\), i.e. \(-2\le x<-\sqrt2\) or \(x>\sqrt2\). For \(x<-2\): \(x^2+2x+2>0\) always. Union: \((-\infty,-\sqrt2)\cup(\sqrt2,\infty)\).

questions.q: If \(\alpha\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)\) then \(\sqrt{x^2+x}+\dfrac{\tan^2\alpha}{\sqrt{x^2+x}}\) is always greater than or equal to
questions.sol: AM–GM: \(\sqrt{x^2+x}+\dfrac{\tan^2\alpha}{\sqrt{x^2+x}}\ge2\sqrt{\tan^2\alpha}=2\tan\alpha\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)=x^3+bx^2+cx+d\) and \(0<b^2<c\), then in \((-\infty,\infty)\)
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=3x^2+2bx+c\) has discriminant \(4(b^2-3c)<0\), so \(f'(x)>0\) for all \(x\).

questions.q: For all \(x\in R\), \(x^2+2ax+10-3a>0\), then the interval in which '\(a\)' lies is
If one root is square of the other root of the equation \(x^2+px+q=0\), then the relation between \(p\) and \(q\) is
questions.sol: \(\alpha+\alpha^2=-p\), \(\alpha^3=q\). Cubing: \(\alpha^3+\alpha^6+3\alpha^3(\alpha+\alpha^2)=-p^3\), i.e. \(q+q^2-3pq=-p^3\).

questions.q: The number of ordered pairs \((\alpha,\beta)\) satisfying of the equation \(\cos(\alpha-\beta)=1\) and \(\cos(\alpha+\beta)=1/e\); \(\alpha,\beta\in[-\pi,\pi]\) is
questions.sol: \(\cos(\alpha-\beta)=1\) gives \(\alpha=\beta\) (the cases \(\alpha-\beta=\pm2\pi\) give \(\alpha+\beta=0\), \(\cos=1\ne\frac1e\)). Then \(\cos2\alpha=\frac1e\) with \(2\alpha\in[-2\pi,2\pi]\) has \(4\) solutions.

questions.q: The second degree polynomial \(f(x)\), satisfying \(f(0)=0\), \(f(1)=1\), \(f'(x)>0\) for all \(x\in[0,1]\) is
Let \(a,b,c\) be the sides of a triangle where \(a\ne b\ne c\) and \(\lambda\in R\). If the roots of the equation \(x^2+2(a+b+c)x+3\lambda(ab+bc+ca)=0\) are real, then
questions.sol: \(D\ge0\): \(\lambda\le\dfrac{(a+b+c)^2}{3(ab+bc+ca)}=\dfrac{a^2+b^2+c^2}{3(ab+bc+ca)}+\dfrac23\). In a triangle \(a^2<a(b+c)\) etc., so \(a^2+b^2+c^2<2(ab+bc+ca)\) and \(\lambda<\frac23+\frac23\).

questions.q: The number of solutions of the pair of equations \(2\sin^2\theta-\cos2\theta=0\), \(2\cos^2\theta-3\sin\theta=0\) in the interval \([0,2\pi]\) is
questions.sol: First: \(4\sin^2\theta=1\), \(\sin\theta=\pm\frac12\). Second: \(2\sin^2\theta+3\sin\theta-2=0\), \(\sin\theta=\frac12\). Common: \(\theta=\frac\pi6,\frac{5\pi}6\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha,\beta\) be the roots of the equation \(x^2-px+r=0\) and \(\alpha/2,2\beta\) be the roots of the equation \(x^2-qx+r=0\). Then the value of \(r\) is
questions.sol: \(\alpha+\beta=p\) and \(\frac\alpha2+2\beta=q\) give \(\beta=\dfrac{2q-p}3\), \(\alpha=\dfrac{2(2p-q)}3\); \(r=\alpha\beta\).

questions.sol: \(q=(\alpha+\beta)^3-3\alpha\beta(\alpha+\beta)=-p^3+3p\,\alpha\beta\), so \(\alpha\beta=\dfrac{p^3+q}{3p}\). Sum of the new roots \(=\dfrac{p^2-2\alpha\beta}{\alpha\beta}=\dfrac{p^3-2q}{p^3+q}\), product \(1\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be the roots of \(x^2-6x-2=0\), with \(\alpha>\beta\). If \(a_n=\alpha^n-\beta^n\) for \(n\ge1\), then the value of \(\dfrac{a_{10}-2a_8}{2a_9}\) is
questions.sol: \(\alpha^2=6\alpha+2\) gives \(\alpha^{10}=6\alpha^9+2\alpha^8\), same for \(\beta\); so \(a_{10}=6a_9+2a_8\) and the ratio is \(3\).

questions.q: A value of \(b\) for which the equations \(x^2+bx-1=0\), \(x^2+x+b=0\), have one root in common is
The quadratic equation \(p(x)=0\) with real coefficients has purely imaginary roots. Then the equation \(p(p(x))=0\) has
opts: two real and two purely imaginary roots
neither real nor purely imaginary roots
questions.sol: \(p(x)=a(x^2+k)\), \(k>0\). \(p(p(x))=0\) needs \(p(x)=\pm i\sqrt k\), i.e. \(x^2=-k\pm\dfrac{i\sqrt k}a\), which is non-real. If \(x\) were real or purely imaginary, \(x^2\) would be real. So the roots are neither.

questions.q: Let \(-\dfrac\pi6<\theta<-\dfrac\pi{12}\). Suppose \(\alpha_1\) and \(\beta_1\) are the roots of the equation \(x^2-2x\sec\theta+1=0\) and \(\alpha_2\) and \(\beta_2\) are the roots of the equation \(x^2+2x\tan\theta-1=0\). If \(\alpha_1>\beta_1\) and \(\alpha_2>\beta_2\), then \(\alpha_1+\beta_2\) equals
questions.sol: Roots: \(\sec\theta\pm\tan\theta\) and \(-\tan\theta\pm\sec\theta\). Here \(\tan\theta<0<\sec\theta\), so \(\alpha_1=\sec\theta-\tan\theta\) and \(\beta_2=-\tan\theta-\sec\theta\). Sum \(=-2\tan\theta\).

questions.q: Suppose \(a,b\) denote the distinct real roots of the quadratic polynomial \(x^2+20x-2020\) and suppose \(c,d\) denote the distinct complex roots of the quadratic polynomial \(x^2-20x+2020\). Then the value of \(ac(a-c)+ad(a-d)+bc(b-c)+bd(b-d)\) is
For real \(x\), the function \(\dfrac{(x-a)(x-b)}{x-c}\) will assume all real values provided
questions.sol: \(y=\dfrac{(x-a)(x-b)}{x-c}\) gives \(x^2-(a+b+y)x+ab+cy=0\). Real \(x\) for every \(y\) needs \(y^2+2(a+b-2c)y+(a-b)^2\ge0\) for all \(y\), i.e. \((a+b-2c)^2-(a-b)^2\le0\), i.e. \((a-c)(b-c)\le0\): \(c\) lies between \(a\) and \(b\).

questions.q: If \(S\) is the set of all real \(x\), such that \(\dfrac{2x-1}{2x^3+3x^2+x}\) is positive, then \(S\) contains
questions.sol: The expression is \(\dfrac{2x-1}{x(2x+1)(x+1)}\), positive on \((-\infty,-1)\cup\left(-\frac12,0\right)\cup\left(\frac12,\infty\right)\). Only (a) and (d) lie inside this set.

questions.q: The equation \(x^{\frac34(\log_2x)^2+\log_2x-\frac54}=\sqrt2\) has
questions.sol: With \(t=\log_2x\): \(t\left(\frac34t^2+t-\frac54\right)=\frac12\), i.e. \(3t^3+4t^2-5t-2=0=(t-1)(t+2)(3t+1)\). So \(x=2,\ \frac14,\ 2^{-1/3}\): three real solutions, exactly one irrational.

questions.q: Let \(S\) be the set of all non-zero real numbers \(\alpha\) such that the quadratic equation \(\alpha x^2-x+\alpha=0\) has two distinct real roots \(x_1\) and \(x_2\) satisfying the inequality \(|x_1-x_2|<1\). Which of the following intervals is(are) a subset(s) of \(S\)?
questions.sol: Distinct real roots: \(1-4\alpha^2>0\), \(|\alpha|<\frac12\). \(|x_1-x_2|=\dfrac{\sqrt{1-4\alpha^2}}{|\alpha|}<1\) gives \(\alpha^2>\frac15\). So \(S=\left(-\frac12,-\frac1{\sqrt5}\right)\cup\left(\frac1{\sqrt5},\frac12\right)\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be the roots of \(x^2-x-1=0\), with \(\alpha>\beta\). For all positive integers \(n\), define \(a_n=\dfrac{\alpha^n-\beta^n}{\alpha-\beta}\), \(n\ge1\), \(b_1=1\) and \(b_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n+1}\), \(n\ge2\). Then which of the following options is/are correct?
questions.sol: \(a_n\) are the Fibonacci numbers (\(a_{n+2}=a_{n+1}+a_n\)), so (c) holds by telescoping \(a_k=a_{k+2}-a_{k+1}\). Using \(\alpha\beta=-1\): \(a_{n-1}+a_{n+1}=\alpha^n+\beta^n\) (b). \(\sum\dfrac{a_n}{10^n}=\dfrac1{\alpha-\beta}\left[\dfrac\alpha{10-\alpha}-\dfrac\beta{10-\beta}\right]=\dfrac{10}{89}\) (a). \(\sum\dfrac{b_n}{10^n}=\dfrac\alpha{10-\alpha}+\dfrac\beta{10-\beta}=\dfrac{12}{89}\), so (d) is false.

questions.q: Let \(\mathbb R^2\) denote \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\). Let \(S=\{(a,b,c):a,b,c\in\mathbb R\) and \(ax^2+2bxy+cy^2>0\) for all \((x,y)\in\mathbb R^2-\{(0,0)\}\}\). Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
opts: For any given \((a,b,c)\in S\), the system of linear equations \(ax+by=1\), \(bx+cy=-1\) has a unique solution.
For any given \((a,b,c)\in S\), the system of linear equations \((a+1)x+by=0\), \(bx+(c+1)y=0\) has a unique solution.
questions.sol: The form is positive definite iff \(a>0\) and \(ac-b^2>0\) (then \(c>0\) too). (a): \(ac=12<b^2=\frac{49}4\), false. (b): \(b^2<\frac14\), true. (c): determinant \(ac-b^2\ne0\), true. (d): determinant \((a+1)(c+1)-b^2=(ac-b^2)+a+c+1>0\), true.

questions.q: Show that the square of \(\dfrac{\sqrt{(26-15\sqrt3)}}{5\sqrt2-\sqrt{(38+5\sqrt3)}}\) is a rational number.
questions.sol: Denominator squared \(=50+38+5\sqrt3-10\sqrt{76+10\sqrt3}\) and \(\sqrt{76+10\sqrt3}=5\sqrt3+1\). So it equals \(88+5\sqrt3-50\sqrt3-10=78-45\sqrt3=3(26-15\sqrt3)\). The square is \(\dfrac{26-15\sqrt3}{3(26-15\sqrt3)}=\dfrac13\).

questions.q: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the roots of the equation \(x^2+px+1=0\); \(\gamma,\delta\) are the roots of \(x^2+qx+1=0\), then \(q^2-p^2=(\alpha-\gamma)(\beta-\gamma)(\alpha+\delta)(\beta+\delta)\).
questions.sol: \((\alpha-\gamma)(\beta-\gamma)=\gamma^2+p\gamma+1=(\gamma^2+q\gamma+1)+(p-q)\gamma=(p-q)\gamma\). \((\alpha+\delta)(\beta+\delta)=\delta^2-p\delta+1=-(p+q)\delta\). Product \(=-(p^2-q^2)\gamma\delta=q^2-p^2\) since \(\gamma\delta=1\).

questions.q: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the roots of \(x^2+px+q=0\) and \(\gamma\) and \(\delta\) are the roots of \(x^2+rx+s=0\), then evaluate \((\alpha-\gamma)(\beta-\gamma)(\alpha-\delta)(\beta-\delta)\) in terms of \(p,q,r\) and \(s\).
questions.sol: \((\alpha-\gamma)(\beta-\gamma)=\gamma^2+p\gamma+q=(p-r)\gamma+(q-s)\) (using \(\gamma^2=-r\gamma-s\)); similarly for \(\delta\). Product \(=(p-r)^2\gamma\delta+(p-r)(q-s)(\gamma+\delta)+(q-s)^2=(p-r)^2s-r(p-r)(q-s)+(q-s)^2\), which simplifies to \((q-s)^2-pqr+sp^2+qr^2-prs\).

questions.q: Show that for any triangle with sides \(a,b,c\) \(3(ab+bc+ca)\le(a+b+c)^2<4(ab+bc+ca)\).
questions.sol: \((a+b+c)^2-3(ab+bc+ca)=\frac12\left[(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2\right]\ge0\). In a triangle \(a<b+c\), so \(a^2<ab+ac\); similarly \(b^2<bc+ba\), \(c^2<ca+cb\). Adding: \(a^2+b^2+c^2<2(ab+bc+ca)\), i.e. \((a+b+c)^2<4(ab+bc+ca)\).

questions.q:
Find the integral solutions of the following systems of inequalities
(i) \(5x-1<(x+1)^2<7x-3\)
(ii) \(\dfrac x{2x+1}\ge\dfrac14\), \(\dfrac{6x}{4x-1}<\dfrac12\)
questions.sol:
(i) \(x^2-3x+2>0\) and \(x^2-5x+4<0\) give \(2<x<4\), so \(x=3\).
(ii) \(\dfrac{2x-1}{4(2x+1)}\ge0\): \(x<-\frac12\) or \(x\ge\frac12\); \(\dfrac{8x+1}{2(4x-1)}<0\): \(-\frac18<x<\frac14\). No common value.

questions.q: For what values of \(m\) does the system of equations \(3x+my=m\), \(2x-5y=20\) has solution satisfying the condition \(x>0\), \(y>0\)
Show that the equation \(e^{\sin x}-e^{-\sin x}-4=0\) has no real solution.
questions.sol: With \(y=e^{\sin x}\): \(y^2-4y-1=0\), \(y=2\pm\sqrt5\). \(2-\sqrt5<0\) is impossible, and \(2+\sqrt5>e\ge e^{\sin x}\). No real solution.

questions.q: \(mn\) squares of equal size are arranged to form a rectangle of dimension \(m\) by \(n\), where \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers. Two square will be called 'neighbours' if they have exactly one common side. A natural number is written in each square such that the number written in any square is the arithmetic mean of the numbers written in its neighbouring squares. Show that this is possible only if all the numbers used are equal.
questions.sol: Let \(k\) be the smallest number written. It is the mean of its neighbours, each \(\ge k\); a mean equal to the minimum forces every neighbour to equal \(k\). Repeating the argument from these neighbours, every square (the rectangle is connected through neighbours) carries \(k\).

questions.q: If one root of the equation \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) is equal to the \(n^{th}\) power of the other, then show that \((ac^n)^{\frac1{n+1}}+(a^nc)^{\frac1{n+1}}+b=0\)
questions.sol: Roots \(\alpha,\alpha^n\): \(\alpha^{n+1}=\frac ca\), so \(\alpha=\left(\frac ca\right)^{\frac1{n+1}}\). \(\alpha+\alpha^n=-\frac ba\) gives \(a\left(\frac ca\right)^{\frac1{n+1}}+a\left(\frac ca\right)^{\frac n{n+1}}+b=0\), i.e. \((a^nc)^{\frac1{n+1}}+(ac^n)^{\frac1{n+1}}+b=0\).

questions.q: Find all real values of \(x\) which satisfy \(x^2-3x+2>0\) and \(x^2-3x-4\le0\).
If \(a>0\), \(b>0\), \(c>0\), prove that \((a+b+c)\left(\dfrac1a+\dfrac1b+\dfrac1c\right)\ge9\)
questions.sol: AM \(\ge\) HM for \(a,b,c\): \(\dfrac{a+b+c}3\ge\dfrac3{\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c}\). Cross-multiplying gives the result.

questions.q:
Consider the system of linear equations in \(x,y,z\)
\((\sin3\theta)x-y+z=0\), \((\cos3\theta)x+4y+3z=0\)
\(2x+7y+7z=0\)
Find the values of \(\theta\) for which this system has non-trivial solutions.
questions.sol: The determinant must vanish: \(7\sin3\theta+(7\cos3\theta-6)+(7\cos3\theta-8)=0\), i.e. \(\sin3\theta+2\cos3\theta=2\). With \(\alpha=\tan^{-1}2\) this is \(\sin(3\theta+\alpha)=\dfrac2{\sqrt5}=\sin\alpha\), so \(3\theta+\alpha=n\pi+(-1)^n\alpha\).

questions.q: For \(a\le0\), determine all real roots of the equation \(x^2-2a|x-a|-3a^2=0\)
questions.sol:
\(x\ge a\): \(x^2-2ax-a^2=0\), \(x=a(1\pm\sqrt2)\); as \(a\le0\) only \(a(1-\sqrt2)\ge a\).
\(x<a\): \(x^2+2ax-5a^2=0\), \(x=a(-1\pm\sqrt6)\); only \(a(\sqrt6-1)<a\).
(The book key lists all four values \(a\pm a\sqrt2\), \(-a\pm a\sqrt6\); only the two above satisfy the case conditions.)

questions.q: Find the set of all \(x\) for which \(\dfrac{2x}{2x^2+5x+2}>\dfrac1{x+1}\)

Let \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\beta_1,\beta_2\) be the roots of \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) and \(px^2+qx+r=0\) respectively. If the system of equations \(\alpha_1y+\alpha_2z=0\) and \(\beta_1y+\beta_2z=0\) has non-trivial solution, then prove that \(\dfrac{b^2}{q^2}=\dfrac{ac}{pr}\)
questions.sol: Non-trivial solution: \(\alpha_1\beta_2=\alpha_2\beta_1\), i.e. \(\dfrac{\alpha_1}{\alpha_2}=\dfrac{\beta_1}{\beta_2}\). Then \(\dfrac{(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)^2}{\alpha_1\alpha_2}=\dfrac{(\beta_1+\beta_2)^2}{\beta_1\beta_2}\), i.e. \(\dfrac{b^2}{ac}=\dfrac{q^2}{pr}\).

questions.q:
Solve the following equation for \(x\)
\(\log_{(2x+3)}(6x^2+23x+21)=4-\log_{(3x+7)}(4x^2+12x+9)\)

questions.sol: If \(x\le-3\) or \(x\ge-1\): \(x^2+6x+8=0\), \(x=-4\) (as \(-2\) is outside). If \(-3<x<-1\): \(x^2+2x-2=0\), \(x=-1-\sqrt3\). (The book key prints only \(-1-\sqrt3\); \(x=-4\) also satisfies the equation.)

questions.q:
Let \(\lambda\) and \(\alpha\) be real. Find the set of all values of \(\lambda\) for which the system of linear equations
\(\lambda x+(\sin\alpha)y+(\cos\alpha)z=0\)
\(x+(\cos\alpha)y+(\sin\alpha)z=0\)
\(-x+(\sin\alpha)y-(\cos\alpha)z=0\)
has a non trivial solution. For \(\lambda=1\), find the value of \(\alpha\).
questions.sol: Determinant \(=-\lambda+\cos2\alpha+\sin2\alpha=0\), so \(\lambda=\sqrt2\cos\left(2\alpha-\frac\pi4\right)\in[-\sqrt2,\sqrt2]\). For \(\lambda=1\): \(2\alpha-\frac\pi4=2n\pi\pm\frac\pi4\), i.e. \(\alpha=n\pi\pm\frac\pi8+\frac\pi8\).

questions.q: Let \(a,b,c\in R\) and \(\alpha,\beta\) be the roots of \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) such that \(\alpha<-1\) and \(\beta>1\) then show that \(1+\dfrac ca+\left|\dfrac ba\right|<0\)
questions.sol: \(g(x)=x^2+\frac bax+\frac ca\) opens upward and both \(-1\) and \(1\) lie between its roots, so \(g(1)<0\) and \(g(-1)<0\): \(1+\frac ca\pm\frac ba<0\), i.e. \(1+\frac ca+\left|\frac ba\right|<0\).

questions.q: Find the set of all solutions of the equation \(2^{|y|}-|2^{y-1}-1|=2^{y-1}+1\)

Let \(a,b,c,d\) be real numbers in G.P. If \(u,v,w\) satisfy the system of equations
\(u+2v+3w=6\)
\(4u+5v+6w=12\)
\(6u+9v=4\)
then show that the roots of the equation \(\left(\dfrac1u+\dfrac1v+\dfrac1w\right)x^2+\left[(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2+(d-b)^2\right]x+u+v+w=0\) and \(20x^2+10(a-d)^2x-9=0\) are reciprocals of each other.
questions.sol: Solving: \(u=-\frac13\), \(v=\frac23\), \(w=\frac53\), so \(\frac1u+\frac1v+\frac1w=-\frac9{10}\), \(u+v+w=2\). For the G.P. \(a,ar,ar^2,ar^3\): \((b-c)^2+(c-a)^2+(d-b)^2=a^2(1-r)^2(1+r+r^2)^2=(a-d)^2\). The first equation is \(9x^2-10(a-d)^2x-20=0\); replacing \(x\) by \(\frac1x\) gives \(20x^2+10(a-d)^2x-9=0\).

questions.q: If \(\alpha,\beta\) are the roots of \(ax^2+bx+c=0\), \((a\ne0)\) and \(\alpha+\delta,\beta+\delta\) are the roots of \(Ax^2+Bx+C=0\), \((A\ne0)\) for some constant \(\delta\), then prove that \(\dfrac{b^2-4ac}{a^2}=\dfrac{B^2-4AC}{A^2}\)
questions.sol: For a quadratic, (difference of roots)\(^2=\dfrac{\text{discriminant}}{(\text{leading coefficient})^2}\). Both equations have the same difference of roots \(\alpha-\beta\).

questions.q: Suppose \(p(x)=a_0+a_1x+a_2x^2+\ldots+a_nx^n\). If \(|p(x)|\le|e^{x-1}-1|\) for all \(x\ge0\), prove that \(|a_1+2a_2+\ldots+na_n|\le1\)
questions.sol: At \(x=1\): \(|p(1)|\le0\), so \(p(1)=0\). Then \(\left|\dfrac{p(x)-p(1)}{x-1}\right|\le\left|\dfrac{e^{x-1}-1}{x-1}\right|\); letting \(x\to1\): \(|p'(1)|\le1\), and \(p'(1)=a_1+2a_2+\ldots+na_n\).

questions.q: For every positive integer \(n\), prove that \(\sqrt{(4n+1)}<\sqrt n+\sqrt{n+1}<\sqrt{(4n+2)}\). Hence or otherwise, prove that \(\left[\sqrt n+\sqrt{(n+1)}\right]=\left[\sqrt{(4n+1)}\right]\) where \([x]\) denotes the greatest integer not exceeding \(x\).
questions.sol:
\((\sqrt n+\sqrt{n+1})^2=2n+1+2\sqrt{n^2+n}\) and \(n<\sqrt{n^2+n}<n+\frac12\), giving \(4n+1<(\sqrt n+\sqrt{n+1})^2<4n+2\).
A perfect square is never of the form \(4n+2\), so no integer \(m\) satisfies \(4n+1<m^2\le4n+2\). Hence \(\sqrt{4n+1}\) and \(\sqrt{4n+2}\) have the same integral part, and so does \(\sqrt n+\sqrt{n+1}\) lying between them.

questions.q: Let \(a,b,c\) be real numbers with \(a\ne0\) and let \(\alpha,\beta\) be the roots of the equation \(ax^2+bx+c=0\). Express the roots of \(a^3x^2+abcx+c^3=0\) in terms of \(\alpha,\beta\).
questions.sol: Dividing by \(a^3\): \(x^2+\frac ba\cdot\frac cax+\left(\frac ca\right)^3=0\), i.e. \(x^2-(\alpha+\beta)\alpha\beta\,x+(\alpha\beta)^3=0\), whose roots are \(\alpha^2\beta\) and \(\alpha\beta^2\).

questions.q: If \(\Delta\) is the area of a triangle with side \(a,b,c\) then show that \(\Delta\le\dfrac14\sqrt{(a+b+c)abc}\). Also show that the equality occurs in the above inequality if and only if \(a=b=c\).
questions.sol: \(\Delta^2=s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)\). By AM–GM on pairs, \((b+c-a)(c+a-b)(a+b-c)\le abc\), i.e. \((s-a)(s-b)(s-c)\le\frac{abc}8\), with equality iff \(a=b=c\). So \(\Delta^2\le\dfrac{(a+b+c)abc}{16}\).

questions.q: If \(x^2+(a-b)x+(1-a-b)=0\) where \(a,b\in R\) then find the values of \(a\) for which equation has unequal real roots for all values of \(b\).
Let \(a\) and \(b\) be the roots of the equation \(x^2-10cx-11d=0\) and those of \(x^2-10ax-11b=0\) are \(c,d\) then find the value of \(a+b+c+d\), when \(a,b,c,d\) are all distinct.
The equation \(2x^2+3x+1=0\) has an irrational root.
questions.sol: \((2x+1)(x+1)=0\): roots \(-\frac12,-1\) are rational.

questions.q: If \(a<b<c<d\), then the roots of the equation \((x-a)(x-c)+2(x-b)(x-d)=0\) are real and distinct.
questions.sol: \(f(a)=2(a-b)(a-d)>0\), \(f(b)=(b-a)(b-c)<0\), \(f(d)=(d-a)(d-c)>0\). \(f\) changes sign in \((a,b)\) and in \((b,d)\): two distinct real roots.

questions.q: If \(P(x)=ax^2+bx+c\) and \(Q(x)=-ax^2+dx+c\), where \(ac\ne0\), then \(P(x)Q(x)\) has at least two real roots.
questions.sol: Discriminants \(b^2-4ac\) and \(d^2+4ac\). As \(ac\ne0\), one of \(-4ac\), \(4ac\) is positive, so at least one quadratic has two real roots.

questions.q: If \(x\) and \(y\) are positive real numbers and \(m\) and \(n\) are any positive integers, then \(\dfrac{x^ny^m}{(1+x^{2n})(1+y^{2m})}>\dfrac14\)
questions.sol: \(1+x^{2n}\ge2x^n\) and \(1+y^{2m}\ge2y^m\), so the expression is \(\le\frac14\).

questions.q: If \(2+i\sqrt3\) is a root of the equation \(x^2+px+q=0\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are real, then \((p,q)=\) ________.
questions.sol: The other root is \(2-i\sqrt3\): sum \(4=-p\), product \(4+3=7=q\).

questions.q: If the product of the roots of the equation \(x^2-3kx+2e^{2\ln k}-1=0\) is \(7\), then the roots are real for \(k=\) ________.
The system of equations \(\lambda x+y+z=0\), \(-x+\lambda y+z=0\), \(-x-y+\lambda z=0\) will have a non zero solution if real values of \(\lambda\) are given by ________.
questions.sol: Determinant \(=\lambda(\lambda^2+1)+(\lambda-1)+(1+\lambda)=\lambda(\lambda^2+3)=0\); the only real value is \(\lambda=0\).

questions.q: The solution of the equation \(\log_7\log_5\left(\sqrt{x+5}+\sqrt x\right)=0\) is ________.
questions.sol: \(\log_5(\sqrt{x+5}+\sqrt x)=1\), so \(\sqrt{x+5}+\sqrt x=5\); then \(\sqrt{x+5}-\sqrt x=1\), \(\sqrt x=2\).

questions.q: If the quadratic equations \(x^2+ax+b=0\) and \(x^2+bx+a=0\) \((a\ne b)\) have a common root, then the numerical value of \(a+b\) is ________.
questions.sol: Subtracting: \((a-b)(x-1)=0\), so the common root is \(1\) and \(1+a+b=0\).

questions.q: There are exactly two distinct linear function, ________ and ________ which maps \((-1,1)\) onto \((0,2)\).
questions.sol: \(y=mx+c\) sends the end points \(-1,1\) to \(0,2\) or to \(2,0\): \(m=1,c=1\) or \(m=-1,c=1\).

questions.q: If \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) are the cube roots of \(p\), \(p<0\), then, for any \(x,y\) and \(z\), \(\dfrac{x\alpha+y\beta+z\gamma}{x\beta+y\gamma+z\alpha}=\) ________.
questions.sol: The cube roots are \(r,r\omega,r\omega^2\) (\(r=p^{1/3}\)). With \(\alpha=r\), \(\beta=r\omega\), \(\gamma=r\omega^2\): denominator \(=r(x\omega+y\omega^2+z)=\omega\cdot r(x+y\omega+z\omega^2)\), so the ratio is \(\frac1\omega=\omega^2\) (with \(\beta,\gamma\) interchanged it is \(\omega\)).

questions.q: If \(x<0\), \(y<0\), \(x+y+\dfrac xy=\dfrac12\) and \((x+y)\dfrac xy=\dfrac{-1}2\), then \(x=\) ________ and \(y=\) ________.
questions.sol: \(u=x+y\), \(v=\frac xy\) are roots of \(2t^2-t-1=0\): \(1,-\frac12\). As \(x+y<0\): \(x+y=-\frac12\), \(\frac xy=1\).

FACT : If \(a\) and \(b\) are rational numbers and \(a+b\sqrt5=0\), then \(a=0=b\).
\(a_{12}=\)
questions.sol: \(\alpha^2=\alpha+1\) gives \(\alpha^{12}=\alpha^{11}+\alpha^{10}\), same for \(\beta\); so \(a_{12}=a_{11}+a_{10}\).

Let \(p,q\) be integers and let \(\alpha,\beta\) be the roots of the equation, \(x^2-x-1=0\), where \(\alpha\ne\beta\). For \(n=0,1,2,\ldots\), let \(a_n=p\alpha^n+q\beta^n\).
FACT : If \(a\) and \(b\) are rational numbers and \(a+b\sqrt5=0\), then \(a=0=b\).
If \(a_4=28\), then \(p+2q=\)
questions.sol: \(\alpha^4=3\alpha+2=\dfrac{7+3\sqrt5}2\), \(\beta^4=\dfrac{7-3\sqrt5}2\). \(a_4=\dfrac{7(p+q)+3\sqrt5(p-q)}2=28\); by the FACT \(p=q\) and \(7p=28\). So \(p=q=4\), \(p+2q=12\).

questions.q:
Let \(a,b,c,p,q\) be real numbers. Suppose \(\alpha, eta\) are the roots of the equation \(x^2+2px+q=0\) and \(\alpha,\dfrac1 eta\) are the roots of the equation \(ax^2+2bx+c=0\), where \( eta^2 otin\{-1,0,1\}\).
Statement - 1 : \((p^2-q)(b^2-ac)\ge0\)
Statement - 2 : \(b e pa\) or \(c e qa\)
opts: Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is a correct explanation of Statement-1
Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is NOT a correct explanation for Statement-1
Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is False
Statement-1 is False, Statement-2 is True.
questions.sol: If \(\alpha\) were non-real, both \(\beta\) and \(\frac1\beta\) would equal \(\bar\alpha\), giving \(\beta^2=1\) — excluded. So all roots are real: \(p^2-q\ge0\) and \(b^2-ac\ge0\); Statement-1 is true. If \(b=pa\) and \(c=qa\) the equations would be identical, forcing \(\beta=\frac1\beta\); so Statement-2 is true, but it does not explain Statement-1.

questions.q: The smallest value of \(k\), for which both the roots of the equation \(x^2-8kx+16(k^2-k+1)=0\) are real, distinct and have values at least \(4\), is

Let \((x,y,z)\) be points with integer coordinates satisfying the system of homogeneous equations: \(3x-y-z=0\); \(-3x+z=0\); \(-3x+2y+z=0\). Then the number of such points for which \(x^2+y^2+z^2\le100\) is
questions.sol: \(z=3x\) and then \(y=0\). \(x^2+9x^2\le100\) gives \(x=-3,\ldots,3\): \(7\) points.

questions.q: For \(x\in\mathbb R\), the number of real roots of the equation \(3x^2-4|x^2-1|+x-1=0\) is ________.

Let \(f(x)=x^4+ax^3+bx^2+c\) be a polynomial with real coefficients such that \(f(1)=-9\). Suppose that \(i\sqrt3\) is a root of the equation \(4x^3+3ax^2+2bx=0\), where \(i=\sqrt{-1}\). If \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3\) and \(\alpha_4\) are all the roots of the equation \(f(x)=0\), then \(|\alpha_1|^2+|\alpha_2|^2+|\alpha_3|^2+|\alpha_4|^2\) is equal to ______.

Let \(a,b,c\) be positive integers in arithmetic progression such that the equation \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) has only integer solutions.
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
opts: Both the roots of the equation \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) are odd integers
If \(b=8\), then \(x=3\) is a root of the equation \(ax^2+bx+c=0\)
questions.sol: Integer roots make \(\dfrac ba=k\) and \(\dfrac ca=m\) integers, and the A.P. gives \(m=2k-1\). \(x^2+kx+2k-1=0\) needs \(k^2-8k+4=n^2\), i.e. \((k-4-n)(k-4+n)=12\): only \(k=8\). So \(b=8a\), \(c=15a\) and the roots are \(-3,-5\). Then \(c-b=7a\); \(c=15\) gives \(a=1\), \(b=8\); \(x=3\) is not a root.
